key_insight: Passive ambient sensing—especially sound—can help predict ICU delirium risk, with the best model reaching AUC 0.80.
clinical_relevance: Environmental monitoring may add an interpretable, low-burden signal to ICU delirium risk assessment and prevention workflows.
method: Analyzed light intensity and sound pressure data from 9 ICUs and 309 patients.
Tested four sequential neural network models across 10 prediction windows.
Used SHAP to explain which features mattered and how they influenced risk.
evidence_signal: The convolutional model performed best, achieving AUC 0.80 on sound-only and combined sound-plus-light data, with sound as the strongest overall predictor.
watch_item: Results come from a modest-sized ICU cohort, so external validation is needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Risk Stratification for ICU Delirium using Pervasive Ambient Sensing Information
